title: Onramp categorization and SLA profiles for VPC and airgapped requests
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Create an operational playbook that categorizes incoming Private/VPC/on-prem (including air-gapped) customer requests into onramp tiers and maps each tier to an SLA profile, required artifacts, and a recommended implementation runway. Goal: reduce time-to-decision on intake, surface risk earlier, and ensure consistent expectations with enterprise customers while protecting engineering capacity.

Key outcomes: 1) A clear tiering rubric (Fast-Track, Standard, Complex) with quantitative thresholds; 2) Three SLA profiles (Response, Scope commit, Delivery runway) tied to tier and contract type; 3) A required-customer-artifact checklist per tier (network diagrams, upgrade windows, compliance attestations); 4) A routing and escalation decision table that maps to Solutions Eng, Customer Success, and Engineering intake queues; 5) Dashboards and telemetry to measure intake-to-triage time and SLA attainment.

Tiering rubric (high level):
- Fast-Track: pre-approved network stack, public-cloud VPC peering only, upgrade matrix matches supported OS/K8s baseline, no airgap, minimal custom integrations. Target SLA: acknowledge 24h, scope-commit 5 business days.
- Standard: standard VPC with limited firewall rules/custom routes, scheduled maintenance window required, may include managed KMS, limited on-prem appliances. Target SLA: acknowledge 48h, scope-commit 10 business days.
- Complex: air-gapped or heavily regulated environments, multi-hop/MPLS, restricted upgrade windows, custom QA/validation, on-prem orchestrator changes. Target SLA: acknowledge 72h, scope-commit 21 business days, delivery runway scoped separately.

Scoring dimensions (quantitative inputs): network-readiness (0-5), upgrade-risk (0-5), airgap-severity (0-5), compliance-overhead (0-5), integration-complexity (0-5). Each ticket gets a composite score used to assign tier programmatically at intake, with guardrails for manual overrides.

Required customer artifacts by tier (examples):
- Network topology diagram (mandatory for Standard+),
- Maintenance/upgrade window matrix (mandatory for all),
- Airgap validation plan and sandbox access (Complex),
- KMS/HSM attestation + allowed cryptographic algorithms (Standard+),
- Contact and escalation list with SOC/NetOps POCs (all tiers).

Routing and SLAs: define per-tier owners, e.g., Fast-Track -> Solutions Eng for rapid config; Standard -> Customer Success + Solutions Eng review; Complex -> Enterprise Solutions + Eng triage. Each route includes an SLA for initial acknowledgement, scope commitment, and an engineer allocation target.

Acceptance criteria for playbook: playbook document published in Confluence, intake form updated to collect scoring inputs, automation rule added to route tickets to the right queue, SLA profiles added to customer-facing docs, and a dashboard created showing intake volume by tier and SLA compliance.

Risks and mitigations: inaccurate customer-provided diagrams can misclassify tier (mitigate with mandatory template and validation checklist); burst of Complex requests could overwhelm Eng (mitigate via commit windows and defined capacity gating); security signoffs delaying progress (mitigate with pre-approved cryptographic and compliance patterns).

Rollout plan: pilot for top 10 enterprise customers over 6 weeks -> iterate rubric -> scale intake automation. Post-pilot metrics and retrospective will inform thresholds and SLA timeboxes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook published to Confluence with tiering rubric and SLA tables; 2) Intake form updated and validated in Sandbox; 3) Automation rule routes new private/VPC/onprem requests to correct queue 80%+ of the time; 4) Dashboard shows baseline metrics (intake-to-triage median under 48h for Standard, SLA attainment reported); 5) Pilot with 5 customers completed and feedback logged.
